I farm sorghum here in the North East like my father did, and last season the rains were not too bad so I got a fair harvest. I have 7.69 hectares in total so I am not the smallest farmer in my village, and since I own this land I put some effort into it. I will buy one bag of NPK and maybe a bag of urea for this 1.71 ha plot if the agro-dealer in town has stock when planting time comes — fertilizer makes sorghum head better here on these tired sandy soils. I will stick with the local sorghum seed I saved from last year because it stands the dry spells better than the new ones, and I cannot waste money on hybrid seed for sorghum when my own seed works. No irrigation here, this is rainfed land, and I will spray a little for the stem borer if I see them coming on the young plants.
